name: The Lost Ingots
summary: Glorin Steelbrow needs Lightforge iron from a shipwreck off the Wetlands. The chest holds only one ingot, and the Bluegill murlocs have taken the rest.

sections.title: A Plundered Shipwreck
sections.body: The Flying Osprey lies broken off the Wetlands shore. Glorin Steelbrow, a dwarven priest, sent you to recover its Lightforge iron. The waterlogged chest in the cargo hold holds only a single ingot. Bluegill murlocs near the wreck have scavenged the rest of the shipment.

sections.title: Reclaiming the Sacred Metal
sections.body: Lightforge iron is rare metal suited to sacred smithing. Glorin Steelbrow needs it for a weapon, so the bars cannot be left in Bluegill camps. Hunt the Bluegill raiders in the shallows near the broken hull and reclaim the scattered ingots for Glorin.

faq.q: What ship carried the Lightforge iron?
faq.answer: The Flying Osprey carried the Lightforge iron before it sank off the Wetlands coast. Its broken timbers lie partly submerged in the shallows.

faq.q: Why were the ingots not in the chest?
faq.answer: Only one ingot remained in the waterlogged chest. Bluegill murlocs had scavenged the rest of the shipment from the wreck.

Glorin Steelbrow is a dwarven priest of the Church of the Holy Light in the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. A colleague of Bishop Farthing, he seeks Lightforge iron for a weapon to use against the necromancer Morbent Fel.

faq.q: What is special about Lightforge iron?
faq.answer: Lightforge iron is rare metal suited to holy enchantments and sacred smithing. Artisans use it to craft weapons aligned with the Holy Light.
Bluegill murloc raiders took the missing bars. They prowl the shallows and beaches around the Flying Osprey wreck.

faq.q: What comes next after returning the ingots?
faq.answer: After Glorin Steelbrow receives all the ingots, he packs the sanctified metal in a crate and sends you to weaponsmith Grimand Elmore in Stormwind. There, the metal is forged in Blessed Arm.

angles.text: As a dwarf, recovering lost masterwork ore for a dwarven priest like Glorin Steelbrow honors your people's tradition of craftsmanship and reclaiming what was lost.
As a paladin, recovering Lightforge iron helps preserve holy metal for weapons that champion the Light.
As a blacksmith, you know the loss of fine Lightforge iron to a coastal murloc nest, where it lies unused instead of being worked at an anvil.
